name: mysqld_exporter-11da31c9-blind30-ots
instr:
# MySQL metrics exporter reporting wrong and missing numbers, without a test suite

This program is pointed at a database server, asks it a fixed list of questions, and turns the answers into named numbers a monitoring system pulls over HTTP. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything that looked wrong when it was aimed at a stub server that answers each of its queries with known rows.

The commonest complaint is silence. Whole families of readings that used to be published now arrive completely empty: the query still goes to the server, the call reports success, and not one sample comes back. That is true of the timestamps each worker thread publishes for the changes it is replaying, the last-applied and currently-applying commit, start and end times per channel and worker id. It is true of the allocation figures per kind of allocation: bytes allocated, bytes freed, bytes currently in use. It is true of the transaction counters a clustered member keeps — queued, checked, conflicts detected, rows validating, remotely applied, locally proposed, rolled back — and of the one-gauge-per-member listing carrying host, port, state and, on newer servers, role and version labels, in both its newer seven-column form and its older five-column form.

More readings have gone the same way. The type/name/value listing that the secondary, log-structured storage back end answers with, including non-numeric entries such as a library version or a date,
